topic.title: Tough Logic Puzzles
topic.description: Complex macro expansions, tricky operator precedence, multi-dimensional structures, and bitwise math.

questions.title: Macro Side Effects
questions.explanation: Macros perform literal text substitution. SQUARE(a + 1) expands to a + 1 * a + 1. Due to operator precedence, this is 3 + (1 * 3) + 1 = 3 + 3 + 1 = 7. It does NOT evaluate as (a+1)*(a+1).

questions.title: Macro Post-Increment
questions.explanation: The macro expands to ((x++) > (y++) ? (x++) : (y++)). Initially x=2, y=3. 2 > 3 is false. y is incremented to 4. x is incremented to 3. The ternary evaluates the false branch: (y++). It evaluates to 4, then y increments to 5.

questions.title: Bitwise XOR Swap
questions.explanation: This is the classic XOR swap algorithm. It swaps the values of a and b without using a temporary variable.

questions.title: Shift Operator Precedence
questions.explanation: Addition (+) has higher precedence than the bitwise shift operator (<<). So it evaluates as x << (1 + 2) -> 1 << 3, which is 8.

questions.title: Bitwise AND with Negation
questions.explanation: In two's complement, -x is equivalent to ~x + 1. The expression x & -x isolates the lowest set bit of x. For 4 (binary 100), the lowest set bit is 4.

questions.title: Array of Function Pointers
questions.explanation: arr is an array of 2 pointers to functions returning int. arr[0]() calls f1 returning 1. arr[1]() calls f2 returning 2. 1 + 2 = 3.

questions.title: Chained Assignments and Side Effects
questions.explanation: b += 2 makes b=4. c *= 2 makes c=6. a becomes 4 + 6 = 10. The output is 10, 4, 6.

questions.title: Logical NOT on Integers
questions.explanation: 5 is non-zero (true). !5 is 0 (false). !!5 is !0 which is 1 (true).

questions.title: Sizeof String Literals vs Pointers
questions.explanation: arr is a character array of size 3 (H, i, \0). ptr is a pointer, whose size is typically 8 bytes on a 64-bit system. 3 is not equal to 8, so it prints 0.

questions.title: Struct Padding Alignment
questions.explanation: c takes 1 byte, followed by 1 byte of padding to align the short on a 2-byte boundary. s takes 2 bytes. i takes 4 bytes. Total: 1+1+2+4 = 8 bytes.

questions.title: Dangling Reference
questions.explanation: get() returns a reference to a local variable x. When get() returns, x is destroyed, leaving a dangling reference. Using it causes Undefined Behavior.

questions.title: Static Cast to Void
questions.explanation: Casting an expression to void evaluates the expression and discards the result. x++ is evaluated, so x becomes 6.

questions.title: Pointer Subtraction Types
questions.explanation: Pointer subtraction returns the number of elements between them, not the number of bytes. 3 - 1 = 2 elements of type int.

questions.title: Virtual Function Default Argument Bind
questions.explanation: Default arguments are bound at compile-time based on the static type of the pointer (B), which provides 1. The function is called dynamically (D::f), which prints the bound argument 1.

questions.title: Switch Case Initialization
questions.explanation: You cannot declare and initialize a variable inside a switch case without creating a scope (using braces {}). The compiler will throw an error because 'x' would be in scope for case 2 but skipped initialization.

questions.title: Operator Precedence with Pointers
questions.explanation: Postfix ++ has higher precedence than *. So *p++ evaluates as *(p++). It returns the original value pointed to by p (10), and then increments the pointer to point to 20.

questions.title: Enum Scope
questions.explanation: Standard enums leak their enumerators into the surrounding scope. Defining RED in Traffic conflicts with RED in Color. This is why enum classes (scoped enums) were introduced in C++11.

questions.title: Const Member Initialization
questions.explanation: Const member variables must be initialized using a member initializer list. They cannot be assigned inside the constructor body.

questions.title: Empty String Length
questions.explanation: strlen stops at the first null terminator, so it returns 0. sizeof evaluates the entire array size: \0, H, e, l, l, o, and the implicit \0 at the end (7 bytes total).

questions.title: Float Equality Comparison
questions.explanation: 0.1f is a float, which lacks precision compared to the double literal 0.1. When compared, the float is promoted to double, but their underlying binary representations are different, making them unequal.

questions.title: String Literal Modification
questions.explanation: String literals are stored in read-only memory. Attempting to modify them through a non-const pointer leads to Undefined Behavior (usually a segmentation fault).

questions.title: Main Function Return
questions.explanation: In C++, it is not strictly required for the main function to have a 'return 0;' statement. If omitted, the compiler implicitly inserts it.

questions.title: Type Promotion in Ternary
questions.explanation: The ternary operator requires both branches to yield a common type. The int 'a' is promoted to double to match 'b'. Thus, 'res' is deduced as a double (8 bytes).

questions.title: Multi-dimensional Array Initialization
questions.explanation: The array is initialized sequentially. arr[0][0]=1, arr[0][1]=2, arr[1][0]=3. Any uninitialized elements in a brace-enclosed list are value-initialized to 0. So arr[1][1]=0.

questions.title: Pointer Comparison
questions.explanation: Pointers to elements within the same array can be compared. Since elements are contiguous in memory and array indices grow upwards, p1 is strictly less than p2.
